title: “the two anointed ones” — who are they?
summary: Zechariah 4:14 answers the question about the two olive trees and the two olive branches with “These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.” The verse does not name them.
text: KJV Zechariah 4:14: “These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth”. KJV Zechariah 4:3: “two olive trees by it”. KJV Zechariah 4:12: “What be these two olive branches which through the two golden pipes empty the golden oil out of themselves”.
reasoning: The prophet asks twice what the two olive trees and the two olive branches are (4:11–12) and is told at 4:14 that they are “the two anointed ones”. The chapter names Zerubbabel at 4:6–10 and the book names Joshua the high priest at 3:1, but 4:14 does not name the two, and the chapter does not say that the two anointed ones are those men. Possible readings, named only as readings: Zerubbabel and Joshua; a king and a priest as offices; two figures of the Lord’s anointing without an identity. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the verses quoted. The record does not say that any reading is the right one, does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek, and does not claim that no other passage says more.

title: “a woman that sitteth in the midst of the ephah” — who or what is she?
summary: Zechariah 5:7–8 has a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah, told “This is wickedness”, and 5:11 has the ephah carried to build it a house in the land of Shinar. The passage does not say who or what she is.
text: KJV Zechariah 5:7: “this is a woman that sitteth in the midst of the ephah”. KJV Zechariah 5:8: “This is wickedness”. KJV Zechariah 5:11: “To build it an house in the land of Shinar”.
reasoning: The angel says of the woman only “This is wickedness” and has her put back and sealed under a talent of lead. The passage does not say whether she is a person, a people, or a figure of a thing, and does not say why the house is built in the land of Shinar. Possible readings, named only as readings: wickedness personified; a figure of a particular people’s or city’s sin; an unnamed figure without a referent. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the verses quoted. The record does not say that any reading is the right one, does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek (the Greek of 5:6 prints a different noun for the ephah and is the subject of a separate T record), and does not claim that no other passage says more.

title: “he hath bid his guests” — who is the sacrifice and who are the guests?
summary: Zephaniah 1:7 has the Lord prepare “a sacrifice” and bid “his guests”, and 1:8 names “the day of the Lord’s sacrifice”. The verses do not say what the sacrifice is or who the guests are.
text: KJV Zephaniah 1:7: “the Lord hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests”. KJV Zephaniah 1:8: “in the day of the Lord's sacrifice, that I will punish the princes”.
reasoning: The sacrifice is prepared by the Lord and the guests are bidden by him, and the next verse describes a punishing of princes, the king’s children and those in strange apparel on “the day of the Lord’s sacrifice”. The passage does not say what is sacrificed, whether the guests are those who will be judged or those who will carry it out, or whether the sacrifice is a figure for the judgment itself. Possible readings, named only as readings: the judged themselves as the sacrifice and a hostile nation as the guests; a sacrificial feast as a figure for the day of the Lord; a particular event not named in the verse. The record does not decide between them.
